# TypeScript

- **[HAR-TS-001] MUST — Repository contract.** Follow the checked-in package manager, workspace boundaries, compiler settings, lint rules, and test runner. Prefer existing types and components over parallel local abstractions; verify typecheck and the affected test/build path.
- **[HAR-TS-002] SHOULD — TypeScript identifier case.** Use `camelCase` for variables, functions, and methods, `PascalCase` for classes, types, interfaces, enums, and React components, and `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` only for true constants such as fixed configuration values; do not prefix interfaces with `I`.
- **[HAR-TS-003] SHOULD — TypeScript intent names.** Name functions with verb phrases (`fetchInvoices`, `formatDate`) and Booleans as predicates with `is`, `has`, `can`, or `should` (`isLoading`, `hasAccess`).
- **[HAR-TS-004] SHOULD — TypeScript file names.** Follow the framework's file conventions, such as Next.js App Router reserved files (`page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `route.ts`), kebab-case route segments, `[param]` dynamic segments, and `(group)` route groups; elsewhere keep the file casing the repository already uses.

# agent-runtime

- **[TOUCH-AGENT-001] MUST — Keep each runtime independently locked.** Claude and Codex runtime packages retain their own committed lockfiles and must not float dependencies during an unattended run.
- **[TOUCH-AGENT-002] MUST — Preserve the engine boundary.** Runtime adapters translate the shared Touchstone candidate contract without moving verification, publishing authority, or another engine's credential into the model process.
